title: A symmetric kernel certificate for Hetyei's second-kind interval transform: a refutation of the kernel conjecture (Discrete Comput. Geom. 2024, Conjecture 39)
beyond_target: accepted after the campaign target of 40 was reached (additional result #50 toward 60)
exact_endpoint: Hetyei347230.kernel_conjecture_false : ¬ Hetyei347230.KernelConjecture, where KernelConjecture := for all n >= 1, deg n ⊓ ker I2 = anti n, with I2(u) = u + u* + sum M(u_(1)*, u_(2)) (Theorem 32) for the Ehrenborg-Readdy coproduct and mixing operator (base cases u a v and v b u, recursion by Nat.rec, proved finite range), deg n the span of length-n ab-words and anti n = {u in deg n : u* = -u}; witnessed by an explicit 20-term symmetric degree-5 element in the kernel
scope: Hetyei's kernel conjecture fails at n = 5 (dim ker I_2 = 13 > 12 = dim A_5) and, computationally, at n = 6, 7; it holds for n <= 4; 347231 (Conjecture 40) fails as a remark, without separate credit
source_targets: Hetyei, arXiv:2007.07362 Conjecture 5.14 = Discrete Comput. Geom. 71 (2024) 918-944 Conjecture 39

root_independent_check: hetyei-root-check-r1/check.py: certificate symmetric, nonzero and in the kernel; kernel and antisymmetric dimensions for n = 1..6

substantive_reason: It refutes a stated structural conjecture in a refereed paper on the kernel of the second-kind interval transform of graded posets, with an explicit symmetric kernel element at degree 5 and a growing excess (1, 2, 7 at n = 5, 6, 7), under the reading of the mixing operator that makes the source's own theorems true; the degree-5 operator agrees with the poset construction on a spanning set. Significance is modest (an exact rank computation the author did not run).

the poset-level identification is a bounded degree <= 5 test, not a formal theorem
